blocks.text: The path of a charged particle is determined by the electric field in the region. The path is typically straight if the field is uniform and the charged particle is moving along the field. However, if a charged particle enters perpendicularly into the uniform field between oppositely charged parallel plates with a certain velocity (Fig. 9.18), it will not go straight. Its path will be parabolic, just like a projectile thrown horizontally in the gravitational field: the horizontal component of the velocity of the charged particle remains constant, whereas the vertical component is accelerated by the electric force.

Figure 9.18 shows that a positively charged particle is attracted towards the negatively charged plate and thus undergoes deflection in that direction. On the other hand, a negatively charged particle is attracted towards the positively charged plate and is deflected in that direction.

blocks.prompt: A positive and a negative particle enter the field between horizontal plates (positive plate on top) moving horizontally. Describe their paths.
blocks.explanation: Each keeps its horizontal velocity while the electric force changes its vertical velocity uniformly, so each follows a parabola. The positive particle bends down towards the negative plate; the negative particle bends up towards the positive plate. A particle moving along the field lines instead goes in a straight line, speeding up or slowing down.

items: Moving along a uniform field: straight path. Entering across the field: parabolic path like a horizontal projectile, horizontal velocity constant, vertical velocity accelerated; positive charges bend to the negative plate, negative charges to the positive plate.
